zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 1; they obstruct downward and outboard views from oceanview and balcony cabins on Decks 4, 5, and 6, with Deck 4 typically most affected.
zones.effect: You'll see the lifeboat equipment when looking down or out, though horizon views remain clear if you look straight out or up; balconies feel less open.
zones.mattersTo: Matters greatly to first-time cruisers or those who want unobstructed water views; experienced cruisers often don't mind since the horizon is still visible and these cabins usually cost less.

zones.what: Lido Deck pool area, buffet, and outdoor activities are directly above on Deck 9.
zones.effect: Expect noise from deck chairs scraping, music, announcements, and foot traffic from early morning through late evening; occasional water dripping from pool deck.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers and anyone planning to nap or turn in early should avoid; doesn't bother those who are out enjoying the ship during the day.

zones.what: Main theater (Pharaoh's Palace) is located on Decks 6-7 forward.
zones.effect: Late-night shows can generate noise and vibration from sound systems and audience activity until around 11 PM; hallway traffic before and after performances.
zones.mattersTo: Affects early-to-bed guests in cabins on Deck 5 forward (below the theater) and Deck 6 forward (same level); won't disturb those out late or heavy sleepers.

zones.what: Main theater (Pharaoh's Palace) seating is two decks below on Deck 6.
zones.effect: Generally quiet — theaters below don't transmit much noise upward through modern insulation.
zones.mattersTo: Not a concern for most guests; structural isolation makes this a non-issue.

zones.what: Elevator banks are positioned forward, midship, and aft on Spirit class, with midship banks serving as the main traffic hubs near the atrium.
zones.effect: Cabins directly adjacent to elevator lobbies experience door chimes, conversation, and foot traffic at all hours; trade-off is convenient access to stairs and elevators.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers who should avoid cabins immediately next to elevator/stair alcoves; doesn't bother guests who prioritize convenience and aren't noise-sensitive.

zones.what: Main engine room is located low and aft; propulsion vibration and low-frequency hum are most noticeable in the aftmost cabins on the lowest guest decks.
zones.effect: A subtle vibration and mechanical hum, especially noticeable when the ship is at speed or maneuvering; some find it soothing (like white noise), others find it intrusive.
zones.mattersTo: Vibration-sensitive guests and light sleepers should avoid; doesn't bother those who sleep through background noise or actually like the engine hum.

zones.what: Bow thrusters operate from the lowest forward section during docking and maneuvering in port.
zones.effect: Loud mechanical grinding and vibration during thruster use, typically early morning arrival and evening departure; lasts 10-30 minutes per use.
zones.mattersTo: Highly disruptive to anyone sleeping in during port arrival; won't matter if you're an early riser or already up on deck.

zones.what: Anchor chain locker is located in the bow; chain deployment and retrieval create loud rumbling every port arrival morning.
zones.effect: Very loud metallic thunder early in the morning (often 6-7 AM) as the anchor drops or is raised; brief but unmistakable wake-up call.
zones.mattersTo: Anyone who wants to sleep in on port days should absolutely avoid; early risers won't care since they're already awake.

zones.what: Main crew corridor (I-95) runs the length of Deck 1 with multiple access points throughout; crew traffic is heaviest during shift changes and early morning services.
zones.effect: Metal doors clanging, crew conversation, and foot traffic at all hours but especially 5-7 AM and during evening turndown; some cabins have crew doors very close.
zones.mattersTo: Light sleepers should avoid Deck 1 cabins near crew access points; heavy sleepers and those out of the cabin most of the day won't notice.
